messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED #incidents — High error rate detected for hosted inference (us-west-2). Trigger: 5xx > 2% and latency p95 > 1.2s. Incident ID: INC-2026-042. Please acknowledge.

maria (oncall): ack. I’m on it — investigating routing and model-serving pods in us-west.

maria (oncall): quick summary for the thread: since ~12:12 UTC we’re seeing elevated 5xx for text-generation routes routed to infer-ash-2. Root cause unknown, replication across replicas. Customers may see failed requests or timeouts. Temporarily routing to fallback model reduces errors.

daniel (sre): on call as backup. Can you paste the error logs? I’ll check autoscaler events and recent deploys.

maria (oncall): logs snippet:
```
2026-02-14T12:13:01Z error: grpc: stream terminated with status UNAVAILABLE
2026-02-14T12:13:02Z warn: KV cache miss spike, inflight queue length 120
2026-02-14T12:13:04Z error: kernel launch failed: out of memory
```
Rolling back a small router config from today didn’t change it. Autoscaler shows some OOM evictions on node pool ash-gpu-1.

kevin (prodeng): looks like a noisy node pool. If fallback routing reduces customer impact, we should publish an initial status update ASAP and set routing to previously healthy pool. Draft below for status page, plz review:

status-bot: suggested status page draft (initial):
```
We are investigating elevated errors and timeouts affecting hosted inference in the US-West region. Impact: a subset of requests to text-generation endpoints may fail or experience increased latency. Mitigation: routing to a fallback model pool has been applied for some customers; our engineers are investigating autoscaler and node health. Next update: in 15 minutes. Incident ID: INC-2026-042.
```

maria (oncall): wording looks good. Two small tweaks: call out that embeddings and non-text endpoints are NOT impacted, and avoid technical terms like 'router' to keep customer-facing. Proposed change:

```
We are investigating elevated errors and timeouts affecting hosted text-generation endpoints in the US-West region. Embeddings and other API surfaces are not impacted. Mitigation: traffic is being routed to a fallback capacity pool to reduce failures for affected customers. Engineers are investigating node health and autoscaling events. Next update: in 15 minutes. Incident ID: INC-2026-042.
```

amy (support-lead): thanks. I’ll prepare a short customer advisory email for paying customers and paste it here once ready. @kevin can you confirm we want to mention "fallback capacity pool" or instead say "alternate capacity"?

kevin (prodeng): prefer "alternate capacity" for clarity to customers.

maria (oncall): updated draft (final for publish) below. Need one sign-off from SRE or ProdEng to publish.

status-bot: ready-to-publish draft:
```
We are investigating elevated errors and timeouts affecting hosted text-generation endpoints in the US-West region. Embeddings and other API surfaces are not impacted. Mitigation: affected traffic is being routed to an alternate capacity pool which reduces request failures for most customers. Engineers are investigating node health and autoscaling events. We will post another update within 15 minutes. Incident ID: INC-2026-042.
```

daniel (sre): lgtm. Go ahead and publish, @status-bot / whoever has access.

maria (oncall): publishing now. Will also add an internal note for customers with active Dedicated contracts to get a targeted message.

status-bot: Published initial status page update at 12:22 UTC. Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-042

amy (support-lead): I’ve drafted the customer email and sent to the affected-custs list. Copy pasted here for records:

```
Subject: Service impact to text-generation in US-West (12:12 UTC)

Hi — we detected elevated errors and timeouts affecting text-generation requests in our US-West region. We have routed traffic to alternate capacity which has reduced failures for most customers. Our engineers are actively investigating and we will provide updates. If you’re seeing persistent issues, reply to this message and we will prioritize.

— Redwood Support
```

kevin (prodeng): thanks Amy. I’ll take over monitoring on call for the next hour. @maria I’ll escalate to infra to check cloud node health and GPU driver versions.

maria (oncall): handing off to @kevin for ongoing ops at 12:28 UTC. I’ll stay reachable for context handover. Note: I increased the autoscaler buffer temporarily which appears to have stabilized p95 latency.

ops-bot: periodic update reminder scheduled in 15 minutes.

(15 minutes later)

kevin (prodeng): periodic update: routing continues to hold, error rate down to 0.6%, p95 latency 890ms. We’re still investigating OOM evictions on ash-gpu-1; infra is replacing 2 nodes. Posting revised status update draft:

```
We implemented routing to alternate capacity which has reduced request failures. Error rate has decreased but some customers may still experience intermittent timeouts. Engineers are replacing unhealthy nodes and continuing to investigate autoscaler behavior. Next update: in 30 minutes or sooner if status changes. Incident ID: INC-2026-042.
```

maria (oncall): +1. Please include a note that Dedicated customers with running jobs may see job restarts — include contact point. Kevin, can you add that? 

kevin (prodeng): added note in the published update at 12:58 UTC. Link unchanged.

(40 minutes later)

daniel (sre): final update: infra reports nodes replaced and GPU driver mismatch fixed on the suspect pool. Error rates stabilized to baseline, no further evictions observed. Recommend resolving and documenting RCA (driver mismatch + autoscaler edge-case with burst launch). Proposed resolved notice:

```
Resolved: The elevated errors and timeouts affecting hosted text-generation endpoints in US-West have been resolved. Root cause: a GPU driver mismatch on a subset of nodes that, combined with an autoscaler timing edge-case, caused OOM evictions and increased request failures. Mitigation: replaced affected nodes, corrected driver versions, and adjusted autoscaler buffer settings to prevent recurrence. Impact: intermittent failures and increased latency between 12:12–13:05 UTC for a subset of customers. No data loss. Incident is now resolved. Incident ID: INC-2026-042. Postmortem will be published within 72 hours.
```

maria (oncall): resolving now. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. I’ll attach logs and timeline to the incident ticket and start the postmortem draft.

status-bot: Published resolved notice at 13:05 UTC. Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-042/resolved

amy (support-lead): notified affected customers that issue is resolved and included steps for reopening a support ticket if they still see problems. :thumbsup:

kevin (prodeng): filing RCA doc and follow-ups for autoscaler guardrail changes. Assigning to infra+runtime teams.

maria (oncall): handoff complete at 13:08 UTC. back to normal ops. :white_check_mark:
